description: The optimisation theory and algorithms that train machine learning models: convex sets and functions, gradient descent and its convergence, stochastic and mini-batch methods, momentum and adaptive methods such as Adam, constrained optimisation with Lagrange multipliers and duality, second-order and quasi-Newton methods, and the practice of tuning and diagnosing training. Every algorithm is derived, implemented from scratch and watched moving across loss surfaces in the browser before it is used on real models.
modelledOn: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning (optimisation chapters)
outcomes: Formulate learning problems as optimisation problems and recognise when they are convex.
Prove and apply the convergence properties of gradient descent under smoothness and strong convexity.
Implement stochastic, mini-batch, momentum and adaptive methods and explain their trade-offs in noise, speed and memory.
Solve constrained problems with Lagrange multipliers, KKT conditions and duality, including the support vector machine.
Apply Newton, quasi-Newton and other second-order methods and judge when their cost is justified.
Diagnose and tune training in practice using learning-rate schedules, gradient checks and loss curves.

units.title: Optimisation problems in machine learning
topics: Empirical risk minimisation as an optimisation problem; loss functions and regularisers
Calculus refresher: gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, directional derivatives and Taylor expansions
Local and global minima, saddle points; first- and second-order optimality conditions
Visualising loss surfaces and level sets for linear regression, logistic regression and small networks

units.title: Convex sets and functions
topics: Convex sets: hyperplanes, half-spaces, balls, polyhedra and cones; operations that preserve convexity
Convex functions: definitions, first- and second-order conditions, Jensen's inequality
Operations that preserve convexity; common convex losses in machine learning
Strong convexity, Lipschitz continuity and smoothness; condition number of a problem
Subgradients and non-smooth convex functions such as the L1 norm and hinge loss
Convex problem classes: least squares, linear and quadratic programming

units.title: Gradient descent and its variants
topics: Gradient descent derived from a quadratic upper bound; step size choice
Convergence rates for smooth convex and strongly convex functions
Line search: exact, backtracking and the Armijo and Wolfe conditions
Ill-conditioning, zig-zagging and the role of feature scaling and preconditioning
Subgradient methods, proximal gradient descent and ISTA for lasso
Coordinate descent

units.title: Stochastic optimisation
topics: Stochastic gradient descent: unbiased gradient estimates and their variance
Mini-batches, sampling with and without replacement, epochs and shuffling
Convergence of SGD with decreasing step sizes; the noise ball
Variance reduction: SVRG and SAGA
Generalisation and the implicit regularisation of SGD; large-batch training
Training on a laptop with limited memory: streaming data and small batches

units.title: Momentum and adaptive methods
topics: Heavy-ball momentum and Nesterov accelerated gradient; optimal rates for first-order methods
Adaptive learning rates: AdaGrad, RMSProp and Adam; bias correction
AdamW and decoupled weight decay; when adaptive methods generalise worse
Comparing optimisers on the same problem and reading their trajectories

units.title: Constrained optimisation and Lagrange multipliers
topics: Equality constraints and Lagrange multipliers; geometric interpretation
Inequality constraints and the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions
Lagrangian duality: the dual function, weak and strong duality, Slater's condition
The support vector machine as a quadratic program; the dual and the kernel trick
Projected gradient descent, penalty and barrier methods; an overview of interior-point methods
Allocating a fertiliser budget across farms as a constrained problem

units.title: Second-order methods
topics: Newton's method: derivation, quadratic convergence and damped Newton
Gauss-Newton and Levenberg-Marquardt for least squares; iteratively reweighted least squares for logistic regression
Quasi-Newton methods: BFGS and limited-memory L-BFGS
Hessian-vector products, conjugate gradient and Hessian-free optimisation
Cost and memory of second-order methods at scale

units.title: Optimisation in practice: tuning and diagnostics
topics: Non-convex optimisation in deep learning: saddle points, plateaus and the loss landscape
Learning-rate schedules: step decay, cosine annealing, warm-up and the learning-rate range test
Initialisation, normalisation and gradient clipping; vanishing and exploding gradients
Diagnostics: gradient checking, loss curves, divergence and NaNs; reproducibility and random seeds
Hyperparameter optimisation: grid, random, Bayesian optimisation and early stopping
Capstone: implementing and benchmarking optimisers on a real model with a written analysis

schedule.title: Learning as optimisation and loss surfaces
schedule.exercise: Write the empirical risk for linear and logistic regression, derive their gradients, and classify the stationary points of a given two-variable function using the Hessian.

tasks.title: Compute the gradient and Hessian of a two-variable quadratic by hand and check the values with symbolic algebra at three points
Classify the stationary points of a given function as minimum, maximum or saddle using the Hessian eigenvalues, and mark them on a contour plot
Plot the loss surface and level sets of logistic regression on a small data set, and describe how regularisation reshapes the minimum

schedule.title: Convex sets and convex functions
schedule.exercise: Proof exercise: show that three given sets are convex and that the sum of two convex functions is convex, and test one function by its Hessian.

tasks.title: Test whether five given one-variable functions are convex by plotting them and checking the second derivative's sign
Check the convexity of squared, logistic, hinge and absolute losses numerically using the Jensen inequality on random point pairs
Prove with symbolic algebra that a given regularised loss is convex, and show the operation rules used at each step

schedule.title: Smoothness, strong convexity and subgradients
schedule.exercise: Compute the Lipschitz constant and strong convexity parameter of a least-squares objective from its data matrix, and the resulting condition number.

tasks.title: Compute a subgradient of the L1 norm and the hinge loss at three points, including a non-differentiable point
Compute smoothness, strong convexity and condition number of a least-squares problem from the eigenvalues of its data matrix
Solve a small quadratic program for a portfolio-style problem with a solver and verify the solution against the optimality conditions

schedule.title: Gradient descent and step sizes
schedule.exercise: Derive the step size 1/L from the quadratic upper bound, and compare constant step and backtracking line search on a given least-squares problem.

tasks.title: Run gradient descent on a quadratic function with three step sizes and plot which converge, oscillate or diverge
Implement backtracking line search with the Armijo condition and compare it with a fixed step on a logistic regression problem
Verify empirically the rate of gradient descent on a smooth convex and a strongly convex problem, and compare with the theoretical bounds

schedule.title: Conditioning, proximal methods and coordinate descent
schedule.exercise: Explain with a two-variable example why poor conditioning slows gradient descent, and how feature scaling or preconditioning changes the iterations needed.

tasks.title: Plot the zig-zag path of gradient descent on an ill-conditioned quadratic before and after scaling the features
Implement ISTA for lasso on synthetic data and show how the number of nonzero coefficients changes along the regularisation path
Compare coordinate descent and gradient descent on a lasso problem for 1000 features, in iterations and time to a fixed accuracy

schedule.title: Stochastic gradient descent
schedule.exercise: Show that a mini-batch gradient is unbiased, derive its variance, and explain the noise ball for a constant step size.

tasks.title: Run SGD with a batch size of 1 on a linear regression problem and plot the loss curve against the full gradient descent curve
Compare batch sizes 1, 16 and 256 on the same problem, with and without shuffling, in loss against epochs and against time
Run SGD with constant and decreasing step sizes, show the noise ball and the convergence under 1/t decay, and fit the observed rates

schedule.title: Variance reduction and training with limited memory
schedule.exercise: Discuss when variance reduction pays off and when plain SGD is enough, and plan how to train a model on a data set that does not fit in memory.

tasks.title: Implement SVRG on a small logistic regression problem and compare its loss curve with plain SGD
Train with small and large batches on the same model and compare their test accuracy to see the effect of large-batch training
Train a classifier on a data set larger than the memory limit, using streaming mini-batches, and report accuracy against memory used

schedule.title: Momentum and adaptive optimisers
schedule.exercise: Write the update rules of heavy-ball, Nesterov, AdaGrad, RMSProp and Adam side by side, and explain when each is likely to help.

tasks.title: Add momentum to gradient descent on an ill-conditioned quadratic and compare the iterations needed with the plain method
Implement AdaGrad, RMSProp and Adam from scratch and compare their paths on a Rosenbrock-style function
Compare five optimisers on the same small network task with tuned learning rates, and write a comparison of speed, final loss and sensitivity

schedule.title: Constrained optimisation and duality
schedule.exercise: Solve a constrained problem with Lagrange multipliers and then with KKT conditions, verifying complementary slackness and the zero duality gap.

tasks.title: Solve a two-variable problem with one equality constraint using Lagrange multipliers and plot the constraint with the contours
Apply the KKT conditions to a problem with two inequality constraints, find which constraints are active, and confirm the solution graphically
Derive the dual of a small quadratic program, compare the primal and dual values, and check Slater's condition for strong duality

schedule.title: SVMs, constrained methods and allocation problems
schedule.exercise: Formulate the allocation of a fertiliser budget across five farms with yield curves as a constrained problem, and solve it.

tasks.title: Apply projected gradient descent to minimise a quadratic function over a box constraint and plot the path
Train a linear support vector machine by solving its dual on 2-D data, and show the support vectors and margin
Allocate a fertiliser budget across five farms with diminishing yield curves by penalty and projected methods, and compare the solutions with a solver

schedule.title: Newton and quasi-Newton methods
schedule.exercise: Do two Newton steps by hand on a two-variable function and compare per-iteration cost and memory with gradient descent for models of 100 and 1 million parameters.

tasks.title: Run Newton's method on a one-variable function and watch the error square at each step, then damp it where it diverges
Fit a logistic regression by iteratively reweighted least squares and compare the iterations with gradient descent
Compare gradient descent, BFGS and L-BFGS on a 1000-parameter problem by iterations, time and memory, and say which wins and why

schedule.title: Optimisation in deep learning
schedule.exercise: Explain in a short note how warm-up, cosine decay and gradient clipping each address a training problem, and set a schedule for a given model.

tasks.title: Train a small network with a constant, a step-decay and a cosine learning rate and plot the three loss curves
Compare weight initialisation schemes on a deep network and measure the gradient norm per layer to show vanishing and exploding gradients
Use the learning-rate range test and warm-up on a deeper network, find the stable range, and explain the loss spikes and plateaus seen

schedule.title: Diagnostics, hyperparameters and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: benchmark at least four optimisers on a real model, with seeds, learning-curve plots, hyperparameter search results and a written analysis.

tasks.title: Check an analytic gradient against a finite-difference gradient and find the bug in a deliberately faulty implementation
Tune the learning rate and weight decay with grid search and random search under the same budget and compare the best results
Benchmark SGD with momentum, Adam and L-BFGS on a real model over five seeds, plot learning curves, and write a short analysis of the results
